title: Website Design in Loves Park, Illinois: A Small Business Guide

cover.alt: Concept illustration of a business owner inspecting web-design portfolios and a mobile service page, not a photograph of a Loves Park office.

figures.title: Inspect a designer's own website
figures.summary: The guide asks buyers to examine visible working evidence before a sales conversation.

items.label: Mobile experience
items.detail: Open the site on a phone and inspect loading, reading, and controls.

items.label: Measured checks
items.detail: Use Lighthouse to inspect performance, accessibility, and SEO findings.

items.label: Keyboard navigation
items.detail: Try reaching links and buttons without a mouse.

items.label: Accessibility information
items.detail: Look for a clear statement and a specific testing approach.

items.label: Maintained content
items.detail: Review whether the published work and information appear cared for.

figures.caption: A practical version of the evaluation steps in this guide; a single score is not a complete assessment.

figures.title: Choose the working relationship the project needs
figures.summary: The article distinguishes delivery needs rather than assuming one provider type fits everyone.

items.label: Agency-style support
items.detail: Consider a team when the project needs marketing production, account management, or multiple stakeholders.

items.label: Direct solo collaboration
items.detail: Consider a solo developer for a defined scope and direct access to the person building it.

items.label: Questions for either
items.detail: Compare the written scope, ownership, evidence, ongoing care, and exit arrangements.

figures.caption: Provider-fit considerations from the article's agency-versus-solo discussion.
